newsitem.title: UK: Level interest rates spark high-yield bond appeal.
newsitem.headline: Level interest rates spark high-yield bond appeal.

text.p: Confidence that interest rates have stabilised at lower levels has prompted a surge of emerging market paper in the Euromarket in the past two weeks.

"Fundamentally because we are in a low interest rate environment across the globe -- particularly in the U.S. and Germany -- there is a comfortable feeling there is little chance of rates going up," a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank said.
"Investors are prepared to take a degree of risk to buy yield."
Despite the more aggressive reoffer levels for emerging market paper, new issues traders said the bonds were "still pretty cheap" while domestic bond yields were relatively expensive.
"We expect to see an aggressive flow of funds into the emerging market sector," one dealer said.

To date this year, around $63.4 billion worth of debt has been raised by emerging market borrowers. This already far excedes the $45.3 billion raised for the whole of last year, Capital DATA Bondware shows.

Another emerging market syndicate manager at a U.S. bank in London said: "Ever since the last employment figures emphasised there would be no hike in U.S. interest rates in the near future, demand has continued for high-yielding paper."
"All deals have been rapidly absorbed - in dollars and other currencies and until there is a sign of a correction in the U.S. Treasury market, we expect the positive mood in the sector to continue."

Traders said emerging market paper spreads had tightened and there was no untoward political uncertainty. "Countries such as Argentina and Mexico are now well under control and people just want to buy the story," one emerging market new issues trader said.
And a Frankfurt-based banker said the motivation behind the flow was: "Yield, yield and yield again."
"And when there are not enough borrowers to match demand, "synthetic' funding is created (such as the recent repackaged bonds)."
He did, however, caution a certain amount of "investor over-exposure" to non-investment grade paper.
